channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iran: Russia and China Deem US Regional Actions Illegal
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that Russia and China consider US unilateral policies responsible for regional developments. Moscow and Beijing oppose Washington's confrontational approach, viewing US actions as illegal and ill-considered. Iran maintains close contact with Russia and China as strategic partners, with ongoing consultations on regional issues.

item.title: Taliban to Attend Upcoming Economic Cooperation Organization Meeting in Iran
item.description: The Taliban announced they will participate in the upcoming Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) meeting in Tehran. This marks a shift from the previous ECO summit in Islamabad, where the Taliban were not invited. The meeting is scheduled for December.

item.title: Kazakh Judoka Yerassyl Kazhybayev to Compete for Bronze in Zagreb
item.description: Kazakhstan's judoka Yerassyl Kazhybayev will compete for a bronze medal at the Grand Prix tournament in Zagreb, Croatia. He will face Saba Inaneishvili of Georgia in the over 100kg category. Aida Toishybekova also competed but was eliminated.

item.title: Iran Rejects Germany's Call to Halt Uranium Enrichment, Cites NPT Rights
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei rejected Germany's demand to stop uranium enrichment, asserting Iran's right under the NPT. He criticized the IAEA's speculation about a new facility and warned that Tehran will respond to any attacks.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Legal Literacy Program in All Schools
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a legal literacy program in all schools, from the first to the eleventh grade. The program aims to promote legal awareness through practical exercises, including guidance on whom to contact and how to seek help when rights are violated. Details are available on daryo.uz.

item.title: ECO Ministerial Meeting Begins in Islamabad Without Afghan Representation
item.description: The 24th ECO Ministerial Meeting commenced in Islamabad, Pakistan, without representatives from Afghanistan. The Taliban's deputy foreign minister implicitly confirmed their non-invitation, stating regional integration without Afghanistan is a 'false dream'. Pakistan's Foreign Ministry confirmed participation from member states' foreign ministers and heads of delegations.

item.title: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan Agree on 100,000 Tons of Potato Exports
item.description: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan have reached an agreement for the export of 100,000 tons of potatoes from the Bamyan province. This deal aims to support Afghan farmers and boost agricultural trade between the two neighboring countries.

item.title: Iran Claims Drone Attack on US Military Base in Bahrain, Responding to US Strike
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for a drone attack on a radar station at a US military base in Bahrain, stating it was retaliation for a US strike on an Iranian communication facility in Sirik. Bahraini authorities reported intercepting multiple objects in their airspace and raised the military's readiness level.

item.title: Taliban Authorities to Meet in Kabul to Discuss Leader's Decrees
item.description: Taliban authorities and supporters are expected to gather at Kabul’s Loya Jirga Hall for a meeting. The meeting aims to promote the implementation of decrees issued by their leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada. Sources within the Taliban confirmed the gathering is scheduled for Monday, Nov. 16.

item.title: Uzbekistan President to Visit Oman on State Visit
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, will visit Oman on November 16–17 at the invitation of Sultan Haitham bin Tarik Al Said. Bilateral high-level negotiations, meetings with major company leaders, and other events will take place in Muscat. The summit agenda includes elevating Uzbek-Omani relations and expanding cooperation in trade, investment, and agriculture.

item.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Claim Drone Attack on US Radar Facility in Bahrain
item.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed it targeted a US radar defense facility at Al-Riffa Air Base in Bahrain using six drones. Anadolu Agency reported that no details were provided about damage or casualties. Bahrain's Interior Ministry had issued warnings prior to the incident. The IRGC also stated the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

item.title: Taliban and Iran Agree to 24-Hour Customs Operations at Border
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Finance announced an agreement with Iran to keep customs offices operating 24 hours a day and increase border crossing capacity. The meeting addressed infrastructure development at the Abu Nasr Farahi crossing and speeding up reconstruction. Discussions also covered the Joint Economic Cooperation Commission and increasing capacity at other border crossings.

item.title: Taliban Plan Gathering to Promote Leader's Decrees, Sources Say
item.description: Taliban authorities and supporters are expected to gather in Kabul to promote the implementation of decrees issued by their leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada. The meeting, scheduled for November 16, will focus on enforcing the leader's directives and discussing a book attributed to him. Security measures have been tightened around the venue.

item.title: UN Launches Second Phase of Economic Recovery Programme with $6 Million Budget
item.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has launched the second phase of its Economic Recovery Programme, funded with $6 million from the Republic of Korea. The initiative aims to support economic recovery in Afghanistan by strengthening livelihoods and rehabilitating social infrastructure in five provinces.

item.title: India Forms Special Units for Potential Border Clashes with China
item.description: India is establishing special units to prepare for potential border clashes with China. Soldiers are being trained for movement and drone surveillance in mountainous regions. Disagreements persist between the two nations over their shared border.

item.title: US Diesel Prices Fall Below $6 Per Gallon, Impact on Kazakhstan Fuel Prices Examined
item.description: US diesel prices have dropped below $6 per gallon for the first time in two months, influenced by falling oil prices and decreased demand. This marks a shift from September's record highs, driven by geopolitical tensions and supply disruptions. The trend's potential impact on Kazakhstan's fuel market is being analyzed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Develops Concept for Disaster Medicine System Enhancement
item.description: Uzbekistan has developed a draft concept for the development of its disaster medicine system. The initiative aims to improve rapid and comprehensive emergency response. International experts from Russia, Turkey, Kazakhstan, WHO, GIZ, and KOFIH, along with local specialists, discussed the concept's significance and implementation.

item.title: Man's body discovered in sewage canal following brutal murder in Kandahar
item.description: The body of a man, identified as Ahmadullah from Daman District, was found in a sewage canal in Kandahar city days after he went missing. Sources reported he was stabbed, set on fire, and his body dumped. His friends allegedly lured him to a party before the murder. Taliban have arrested several suspects.

item.title: Afghanistan and Iran Agree to Boost Trade, Upgrade Border Infrastructure
item.description: Afghanistan and Iran have agreed to strengthen economic cooperation, expand border infrastructure, and improve customs operations. Senior officials met in Tehran to discuss organizing the next Joint Economic Cooperation Commission meeting and accelerating reconstruction at the Abu Nasr Farahi customs crossing. Iran pledged full cooperation in economic and political affairs.

item.title: Taliban Detain Two Shiite Clerics in Herat for Religious Observance
item.description: Reliable sources confirm the Taliban have detained two Shiite clerics, Mohammad Javad Rajabzadeh and Mohammad Ruhani, in Herat province. The clerics, who lead prayers at the Sadiqia Mosque, were reportedly arrested for holding a mourning ceremony for Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad. The reason for their detention remains unclear, but such arrests have occurred previously.

item.title: Israeli Intelligence Warns of Potential Iranian Assassination Attempt on Trump
item.description: Israeli intelligence has reportedly warned of a potential Iranian assassination attempt against Donald Trump. Following this warning, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Pentagon chief Pete Hegset have allegedly been moved to protected facilities, and Trump's public appearances are restricted.

item.title: Taliban Finance Minister Meets with Iranian Foreign Minister
item.description: The Taliban's Finance Minister held a meeting with the Iranian Foreign Minister. The details of their discussions were not immediately available. This meeting signifies ongoing diplomatic engagement between the Taliban administration and neighboring countries.

item.title: Afghanistan's absence from ECO foreign ministers' meeting raises questions
item.description: Afghanistan's absence from the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) foreign ministers' meeting in Islamabad has raised questions. Despite its ECO membership and strategic location, the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan did not participate. Member states are discussing economic cooperation, trade, and connectivity. Analysts warn that excluding Afghanistan could undermine ECO's objectives.

item.title: Uzbekistan Temporarily Halts Phone IMEI Registration Amid Smuggling Schemes
item.description: Uzbekistan's Customs Committee temporarily suspended phone IMEI registration at Tashkent airport due to schemes circumventing duty-free limits. The issue was resolved within a day. The committee also stated that phone import duties will be eliminated upon WTO accession, though VAT will remain. Official phone imports reached 4.1 million units in the first 10 months.

item.title: ASEAN Maintains Restrictions on Myanmar's Military Authorities
item.description: ASEAN leaders decided to adhere to their existing five-point peace plan regarding Myanmar at the Manila summit. Despite proposals to change the approach, no easing of restrictions against the country's military authorities was implemented. The plan includes cessation of violence, dialogue, ASEAN mediation, and humanitarian aid.

item.title: Uzbekistan Recovers Over 832 Billion Soums in Delayed Wages
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Labor Inspectorate recovered over 832 billion soums in delayed wages for nearly 35,000 employees during January-September. The Ministry of Poverty Reduction and Employment reported that over 15,000 inspections identified more than 36,000 labor law violations, with education, construction, industry, and agriculture sectors most affected.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Prohibit Privatization of Land in Educational and Medical Institutions
item.description: Uzbekistan will prohibit the privatization of land located within educational and medical institutions, according to a presidential decree. A draft law is being prepared to implement this measure. Efforts will also be made to increase green spaces in district and city centers to 30%.

item.title: Almaty Shuts Off Water Supply to Non-Compliant Car Washes
item.description: Almaty authorities have disconnected water supply to several car washes for violating operational rules. Investigations revealed that seven car washes lacked essential water recycling systems. These facilities can have their water supply restored only after installing the required equipment and passing inspection.

item.title: COP31 Climate Summit Faces Stalemate Over Future of Fossil Fuels
item.description: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, is facing significant disagreements regarding the future of fossil fuels. Nearly 200 countries are negotiating emission reductions and clean energy transitions, but major oil, gas, and coal producers are resisting strict commitments. Developing nations fear economic growth limitations, while vulnerable island states demand accelerated emission cuts.

item.title: Tashkent Reports 307 New HIV Cases in Nine Months; Sexual Transmission Dominant
item.description: Tashkent has recorded 307 new HIV cases in the first nine months of the year. A significant majority, 75.9%, of these new infections are attributed to sexual transmission. The city has also seen an increase in individuals registered for mental health and addiction services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Transport Minister Reverses Stroller Ban on Public Buses
item.description: Kazakhstan's Transport Minister Assel Zhanasova has decided to review regulations regarding the transport of baby strollers on public buses, aiming to eliminate ambiguous interpretations. The minister emphasized the importance of public transport being convenient and accessible for families with young children, ensuring no parent is forced to leave a bus due to stroller issues.

item.title: New Section of Aktobe-Kandyagash Highway in Kazakhstan Becomes Toll Road
item.description: An 89-kilometer section of the Aktobe-Kandyagash highway, a road of republican significance in Kazakhstan's Aktobe region, has been integrated into the existing Kandyagash-Makat toll road system. The new charges, effective November 15, apply to all vehicle types on a specific segment, with discounts available for local residents and annual passes offered.

item.title: Kremlin's Conditions for Ending War Revealed by Media Reports
item.description: Media reports have revealed the terms under which the Kremlin is prepared to end the war. These new demands reportedly echo Russia's ultimatum to Europe and NATO in late 2021, prior to the full-scale invasion, and are said to apply not only to the EU and NATO but also to Moldova, Finland, and Central Asian countries.

item.title: ASEAN Summit Opens in Manila to Address Geopolitical and Economic Instability
item.description: The 49th ASEAN Summit commenced in Manila, bringing together regional leaders and international partners to discuss the impact of armed conflicts, economic instability, energy security, and rising global tensions. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged unity amidst geopolitical challenges and highlighted the region's interdependence. Territorial disputes in the South China Sea remain a key topic.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to visit Oman for state talks
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will undertake a state visit to Oman, with high-level bilateral negotiations and meetings with major company leaders scheduled in Muscat on November 16-17.

item.title: Taliban forces detain two female health workers in Bamiyan for traveling without guardians
item.description: Taliban forces detained two female health workers in Afghanistan's Bamiyan province for traveling without male guardians. Sources reported they were held for 24 hours, subjected to verbal abuse, and released.

item.title: Kabul Hospital Closed by Justice Minister's Order, Owner Claims
item.description: Jawad Mohseni, owner of Khatam al-Nabieen Hospital, states the facility was shut down by Kabul authorities on the Justice Minister's orders after he refused to hand over management. The hospital provided services for over 15 years, particularly in kidney treatment and urology.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports 1.4 Million Citizens Living in Poverty
item.description: As of October 1, 1.4 million people in Uzbekistan are classified as poor, according to the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction. This represents 3.6% of the population, down from 5.8% at the start of the year when 2.2 million citizens were identified as poor. The ministry focuses on targeted support for each family.

item.title: Turkey Detains 35 Afghan Migrants Attempting to Reach Greece by Sea
item.description: Turkish police apprehended 35 Afghan migrants attempting to cross into Greece by sea in Balikesir province. Four suspects accused of migrant smuggling were also arrested. Police seized life jackets and pumps. The migrants were transferred to a reception center, and three of the four suspects were remanded in custody.

item.title: UK Envoy to Visit Pakistan for Afghanistan-Related Dialogue
item.description: The UK's Special Representative for Afghanistan, Richard Lindsay, will visit Pakistan to discuss regional developments and facilitate dialogue on issues between Afghanistan and Pakistan. He met virtually with Mullah Abdul Wasi, Chief of Staff of the IEA Prime Minister's Office, who thanked the UK for its humanitarian aid and efforts to resolve bilateral issues.
